claims.text: The vLLM paper explains why batching helps: requests in a batch share the same weights, so the cost of moving them is spread across the batch.

claims.text: Their architecture guide describes traditional batching as running a fixed group together and waiting for the slowest request before the next group starts, which leaves the GPU idle between batches.

claims.text: The Orca paper (OSDI 2022) calls this request-level scheduling: a request that finishes early cannot go back to its client until the whole batch is done, and a new request waits until the running batch completes.

claims.text: Orca's fix is iteration-level scheduling: the scheduler runs one iteration of the model at a time over the requests it picks, and returns any finished request to its client right away.

claims.text: Orca's answer is selective batching: operations such as Linear, LayerNorm, Add and GeLU are batched by flattening every request's tokens into one tensor, while attention is split and run per request, because attention must look only at each request's own tokens, and each request has a different number of them.
